questions.q: What is the core difference in scope between Terraform and Bicep?
options: Terraform and Bicep are two names for exactly the same tool
Terraform can provision resources across any cloud provider via swappable provider plugins; Bicep only targets Azure
Both tools only work with Azure and have no meaningful difference
Terraform only works with Azure; Bicep works with any cloud provider
questions.explain: Terraform's provider model makes it cloud-agnostic. Bicep was built by Microsoft specifically and exclusively for Azure.

questions.q: What language does Terraform use to describe infrastructure?
options: HCL (HashiCorp Configuration Language)
Bicep syntax
Raw ARM JSON only
Python
questions.explain: Terraform files are written in HCL, HashiCorp's own declarative configuration language.

questions.q: Why doesn't Bicep need a separate state file the way Terraform does?
options: Bicep doesn't actually create real Azure resources
Bicep compiles to ARM templates, and Azure itself is the source of truth for what's deployed
Terraform's state file is optional and rarely used in practice
Bicep keeps its state file hidden inside the CLI binary
questions.explain: Because Bicep deployments go through Azure Resource Manager, Azure tracks the deployed state — there's no separate file to manage or lose.

questions.q: Which kind of team would most likely standardize on Terraform over Bicep?
options: A team that only ever uses Azure and wants zero state-file overhead
A team that has never used a cloud provider
A team running workloads across Azure and another cloud like AWS or GCP
A team with no infrastructure to provision at all
questions.explain: Terraform's multi-cloud provider model is most valuable when a team actually spans more than one cloud.

questions.q: Why does this course teach both Terraform and Bicep instead of picking one?
options: Because Terraform and Bicep are legally required to be taught together
Because Bicep is being deprecated in favor of Terraform
Because real data engineering teams use both, depending on whether they're Azure-only or multi-cloud
Because Terraform cannot provision any Azure resources at all
questions.explain: Neither tool is universally 'better' — the right choice depends on context, so this course builds real fluency in both.
